reading.body:
Meta's Sarpy County campus has no published power capacity figure, so its scale relative to AI infrastructure elsewhere cannot be measured from operator disclosures. The investment ($2.5B+), timing (groundground 2017), and staffing (300+ operational roles) indicate a hyperscale facility, but without megawatts disclosed, the campus cannot be ranked against other AI compute sites. Nebraska as a state has 21 mapped data center facilities and zero published megawatts from any operator.

Meta states the campus matches its electricity use to 100 percent clean and renewable energy and reports a Meta-supported project adding 320 megawatts of renewable generation in Nebraska, which would be new grid supply tied to this region. The company also reports LEED Gold certification for operational buildings. These commitments address power supply and building efficiency, the two constraints most directly binding AI scaling, though no campus-specific power draw is available to assess the actual density or burden.

Without published capacity, this campus cannot be evaluated as a marginal site in the AI power constraint story. It remains mapped, confirmed through Meta's own fact sheet, and known to represent material investment in Nebraska, but its relevance to AI scaling depends on unpublished figures: the actual megawatts it consumes, the timeline to full operation, and whether the renewable energy additions precede or follow demand from this and other hyperscale loads in the region.
